statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) through every scheduled CME weekend halt hour and 12 to 13 (low) in the three reopen hours; Stress 25 (moderate) now, rising to 47 (elevated) at the reopen; Confidence 60 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in the first twenty-one hours covered here and Tail stays far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs from 25 to 47 as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence eases from 60 to 47 as the Friday reference tape ages before recovering into the reopen when live price discovery would resume. No danger window is published, because no observed one-way structure exists and none can form while the venue is closed.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 29: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%) closed near the low of a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range, NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, and a post-Jackson-Hole repricing that lifted September hike odds to about 56%; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC as the twenty-second slot of this window
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which falls inside this window as its final three slots, so the first twenty-one hours assessed here are a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. The reference tape was re-verified against primary sources this run and was unchanged: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close, finishing near the lower end of that range; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43, down 0.55 percent, within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column, at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, because the 28 August column has not yet been published; verified Friday reporting places the 10-year about 4 basis points higher near 4.72 percent and the 2-year roughly 8 basis points higher after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks, which markets read as leaning toward a September increase and which lifted odds of a 25 basis point hike to about 56 percent from roughly 35 percent the prior day. That repricing remains the single most important item in the current evidence set, and weekend reporting published on 29 August and verified this run adds a materially Tail-limiting detail: longer-dated yields barely moved even as the front end jumped, which is the signature of a rotation rather than of the broad discount-rate repricing that denies mean reversion. The rest of the cross-asset picture is coherent with that reading: gold fell 2.88 percent to 4,529.90 dollars, the semiconductor complex led the drag with the Semiconductors group down about 2.9 percent and Semiconductor Equipment down about 4.0 percent and Technology down about 1.4 percent, yet the Dow finished effectively flat at minus 0.02 percent, Communication Services gained about 1.4 percent and Consumer Cyclical about 1.4 percent, and VIX declined on the day rather than bidding. WTI settled near 83.44 dollars, down about 0.11 percent and roughly 4 percent lower on the week, while verified weekend reporting describes Strait of Hormuz traffic well below normal, a severe assessed maritime risk level and continued rhetorical escalation from the IRGC. That confrontation is a six-month-old condition rather than a new discontinuity, and falling crude into it argues against an energy-driven equity shock, so it is scored as background rather than as a Tail amplifier. Shared delayed cross-asset context was 108 minutes old at assessment time and therefore treated as stale under the freshness rule; it was consulted only as weak confirmation of the verified Friday levels and was never used as live price-path evidence. Tail is therefore published at 5 for every scheduled halt hour, because the persistent no-retracement price path that Tail is defined against cannot form in a market that is not open, and at 13, 13 and 12 for the three scheduled reopen hours, where a weekend gap into thin Sunday-evening liquidity is a genuine but conditional possibility that stays far below the 25 block threshold. Stress rises from 25 to 47 across the window because unpriced weekend information accumulates against a dense 1 to 4 September macro stack that runs from ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday through ADP and the Broadcom results on Wednesday to ISM Services on Thursday and the August payrolls report on Friday. Under the fixed mapping those releases are checkpoints rather than automatic Tail blocks, and no danger window is published because no one-way structure has been observed and none can be observed while the venue is closed.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 01:00 UTC on Saturday 29 August to 00:00 UTC on Sunday 30 August, hours 5 to 28 of the CME weekend halt. The mode was normal in every slot and the mapped policy state never left EA_ON. Tail held the 5 floor in all twenty-four hours, because no venue was open to produce the price-path evidence Tail is defined against. Stress dipped to a 22 trough in the early hours and then rebuilt to a 25 plateau held for the final nineteen slots, while Confidence declined steadily from 83 to 61 as the Friday reference tape aged without any new observation to refresh it. No slot was unavailable and no assessment in the window was revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The first twenty-one hours of this window fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; Tail is held at 5 throughout, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON, and the dominant mode is normal in those slots because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress climbs from 25 to 43 across those hours as unpriced weekend information accumulates against Friday's hawkish repricing and the dense 1 to 4 September macro week, while Confidence decays from 60 to 47 purely through the ageing of the reference tape. The final three slots are the scheduled Globex reopen at 22:00 UTC, the first full hour after it and the hour around the Tokyo cash open, the first hours in this window that can host observable structure: they are published with conditional Tail readings of 13, 13 and 12 and a mixed mode, which allows for a weekend gap into thin Sunday-evening liquidity while remaining far below the 25 block threshold, and with Confidence recovering from 55 to 61 as live price discovery would resume. Whether the reopen matters for Tail will depend on whether early retracements hold rather than on the size of any gap, and no such structure is observed at publication time.

forecast.analysis: Observed as current fact: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and this is halt hour 29, with NQ last printing 29,491.75 at Friday 20:59 UTC. Tail sits at its 5 floor because the persistent no-retracement path it measures cannot form in a closed venue. Stress 25 carries Friday's hawkish repricing forward.
drivers: Globex halted since Friday 21:00 UTC; halt hour 29 of a scheduled 49
September hike odds near 56% after Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks
Tail floor of 5 reflects an absent price path, not an assessed calm tape

forecast.analysis: The venue is scheduled to stay closed through this hour, so the mode is published as normal because a halted market offers no structure to classify rather than because conditions are judged calm. The mapped policy state remains EA_ON for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD, and only Confidence moves as the reference tape ages.
drivers: Scheduled halt continues; the Globex reopen is not until 22:00 UTC
Mode published as normal for want of any classifiable structure
Confidence decays purely from tape age, not from conflicting evidence

forecast.analysis: No new price evidence can arrive during a scheduled halt, so this hour repeats the prior scores. Stress stays at 25 on an unresolved September policy debate rather than on any observable stress in the tape: VIX finished Friday at 14.43, down on the day, which is not the signature of a market bracing for disorder.
drivers: Static evidence set: no venue open to revise the price-path picture
VIX 14.43 and lower on Friday argues against a bracing tape
Stress 25 anchored on the unresolved September Fed policy debate

forecast.analysis: Weekend reporting verified this run notes that long-dated yields barely moved after the Jackson Hole speech even as the two-year jumped about 8 basis points. That front-end concentration limits the Tail case, because a discount-rate shock that stays in the short end is a rotation rather than the broad repricing that denies mean reversion.
drivers: Two-year rose about 8bp Friday while the 10-year added only about 4bp
Front-end concentration reads as rotation, not a broad discount-rate shock
H.15 still carries 27 August as its latest column: 2Y 4.20%, 10Y 4.67%

news.title: Warsh raises stakes for Fed's next meeting, and other takeaways from Jackson Hole conference

forecast.analysis: Friday's decline was led by semiconductors, with the group down about 2.9 percent and semiconductor equipment about 4.0 percent, while the Dow closed effectively flat and Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical both gained. That internal split is the main reason Stress rather than Tail carries the hawkish repricing into this halt hour.
drivers: Semiconductor-led drag: group about -2.9%, semi equipment about -4.0%
Dow effectively flat at -0.02% while two sectors closed higher
A split tape raises Stress and lowers conviction, not Tail

forecast.analysis: Gold fell 2.88 percent to 4,529.90 dollars on Friday alongside the hawkish repricing, a coherent cross-asset signature rather than a disorderly one. During this halt hour that alignment is historical context only; no cross-asset market that trades continuously can revise the Nasdaq-100 picture while the index venue itself is closed.
drivers: Gold -2.88% to 4,529.90 is coherent with a hawkish real-rate impulse
Coherent cross-asset alignment argues against disorderly repricing
Cross-asset context cannot substitute for an absent NQ price path

forecast.analysis: Early Sunday in Asia and still inside the halt. Equity index futures do not trade, so any regional headline that lands in this hour will remain unpriced until the 22:00 UTC reopen rather than producing observable structure. Scores are therefore unchanged and Tail stays at the floor for a twenty-ninth consecutive published hour.
drivers: Asian Sunday hours carry no Nasdaq-100 venue and no price discovery
Any headline landing now stays unpriced until the 22:00 UTC reopen
Tail held at the 5 floor through a full day of halt slots

forecast.analysis: Confidence continues its slow decay through this hour, now at 53 in the medium-low band. The decline is a statement about the age of the Friday reference tape rather than about conflicting evidence: the verified levels themselves were re-checked against primary sources this run and were unchanged.
drivers: Confidence 53 reflects tape age, with no conflicting evidence present
Friday levels re-verified against primary quote pages this run
Medium-low Confidence is expected inside a long scheduled halt

forecast.analysis: The persistent geopolitical backdrop is the Strait of Hormuz confrontation, where verified weekend reporting describes traffic well below normal and a severe assessed risk level. It is a six-month-old condition rather than a new discontinuity, and WTI fell about 4 percent on the week, so it does not lift Tail in this hour.
drivers: Hormuz disruption is a persistent condition, not a fresh discontinuity
WTI settled near 83.44 dollars and lost about 4% on the week
Falling crude into a shipping confrontation argues against contagion

news.title: Strait of Hormuz traffic remains below normal as US sanctions pressure Iran

forecast.analysis: Rhetorical escalation was verified over the weekend, with the IRGC claiming decisive control of the strait, but rhetoric without a supply interruption is not the geopolitical discontinuity that would amplify Tail. Crude's direction remains the discriminating evidence and it points away from an energy-driven equity shock in this hour.
drivers: IRGC claim of decisive control is rhetoric without a supply break
Crude direction, not rhetoric, is the discriminating tail evidence here
No verified interruption to physical supply in the current evidence set

news.title: Iran war updates: IRGC says 'decisive control' over Strait of Hormuz

forecast.analysis: The window now passes the midpoint of the remaining halt. Confidence reaches 50 and Stress is unchanged at 25, because nothing in a closed market can either confirm or contradict the Friday picture. The next genuine information event scheduled in this window is the reopen itself, eleven hours later.
drivers: Halt midpoint reached with the evidence set entirely unchanged
The 22:00 UTC reopen is the next scheduled information event
Stress 25 holds because no observation can move it during a halt

forecast.analysis: Midday Sunday in Europe with no venue open. Confidence is held rather than decayed here because the reference tape's age is only one input and the underlying macro picture, dominated by an unresolved September Fed decision, is stable and well documented across the sources verified this run.
drivers: No European or U.S. venue trades the Nasdaq-100 in this hour
Confidence held rather than decayed on a stable documented macro picture
September Fed decision remains the dominant unresolved variable

news.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming

forecast.analysis: Consumer prices were reported up 3.4 percent over the twelve months to July, with the Fed's preferred measure at 3.7 percent, which is the published basis for the hawkish shift. Those are known figures rather than pending releases, so they inform Stress in this halt hour and cannot generate a price path while the venue is closed.
drivers: Verified inflation basis: CPI 3.4% y/y, preferred measure 3.7% y/y
Known published figures inform Stress rather than create Tail
No release is scheduled inside this hour

news.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming

forecast.analysis: Attention in the second half of the window turns toward the macro calendar that opens on Tuesday with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS. Those are scheduled checkpoints two days beyond this hour, not events in it, and under the fixed mapping a checkpoint is not a Tail block. Scores are unchanged for this halt slot.
drivers: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September are scheduled checkpoints
Calendar items outside the window cannot move this hour's Tail
Monday carries only the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 14:30 UTC

forecast.analysis: Stress begins to tick up from 25 as the window approaches the reopen and the quantity of weekend information that has not yet been priced accumulates. Tail is deliberately not moved with it: unpriced information is a dispersion problem, and dispersion is scored as Stress until an actual price path shows mean reversion failing.
drivers: Stress starts rising on accumulating unpriced weekend information
Dispersion is scored as Stress, not Tail, before any path is observed
Tail unchanged at 5 with seven halt hours still scheduled

forecast.analysis: A second small Stress increment for the same reason. The reopen is now six hours away and the practical question it poses is a gap of unknown size against a Friday close of 29,491.75 in NQ. Gap size on its own is a Stress input; only the behaviour of retracements after the gap would be Tail evidence.
drivers: Reopen six hours out against a 29,491.75 NQ Friday reference
Gap size is a Stress input; retracement behaviour would be Tail evidence
No observed structure exists to support any directional lean

forecast.analysis: Stress reaches 29 in the late European afternoon. The composition of the risk is unusually clear for a weekend: one dominant unresolved policy question, one persistent but non-accelerating geopolitical condition, and a dense U.S. data week beginning Tuesday. None of the three has produced observable one-way structure.
drivers: Three-part risk composition: policy, Hormuz, and a dense data week
None of the three has produced observable one-way Nasdaq-100 structure
Stress 29 sits comfortably inside the moderate band

news.title: Strait of Hormuz traffic remains below normal as US sanctions pressure Iran

forecast.analysis: Confidence eases to 47 while Stress advances to 32, the characteristic shape of the hours immediately before a venue reopens: the stored evidence is at its oldest and the amount of information waiting to be priced is at its largest. The venue is still closed for the whole of this hour, so Tail remains at the floor.
drivers: Pre-reopen shape: oldest stored evidence, largest unpriced backlog
Venue closed for the whole hour keeps Tail pinned at 5
Stress 32 and Confidence 47 both reflect proximity to the reopen

forecast.analysis: Three hours before the scheduled reopen, Stress reaches 35. The published Stress path is an explicit statement that a difficult or high-volatility environment can be anticipated while the pathological price path Tail measures cannot be, because the latter requires observation and no observation is possible in a closed market.
drivers: Stress can be anticipated; the Tail price path can only be observed
Three hours remain until the scheduled 22:00 UTC Globex reopen
Mapped policy state stays EA_ON across every halt hour

forecast.analysis: Stress reaches 39 in the penultimate pair of halt hours, still inside the moderate band. Sunday-evening reopens are typically thin, and thin liquidity is the mechanism by which a modest amount of unpriced information can produce a disproportionate first print without implying that retracements will fail afterwards.
drivers: Thin Sunday-evening liquidity can exaggerate a first print
An exaggerated first print does not by itself imply failed retracements
Stress 39 remains inside the moderate band ahead of the reopen

forecast.analysis: The final scheduled halt hour, hour 49 of 49. Stress at 43 sits near the top of the moderate band and combines Friday's hawkish repricing, a semiconductor-led drag and the 1 to 4 September macro stack. Tail is still 5 because the venue remains closed for the whole of this hour.
drivers: Final scheduled halt hour before the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen
Stress near the top of the moderate band on repricing plus a data week
Tail remains 5 because no venue trades during this hour

forecast.analysis: The scheduled Globex reopen falls in this hour, the first slot in the window able to host observable structure. Tail is published conditionally at 13 to allow for a weekend gap into thin Sunday-evening liquidity while remaining far below the 25 block threshold. The mode is mixed because direction is genuinely unresolved.
drivers: Globex scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC; first slot able to host structure
Conditional Tail of 13 allows for a gap into thin early liquidity
Mode mixed because reopen direction is unresolved, not because of chop
Confidence recovers to 55 as live price discovery would resume

news.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq end week on down note as rate-hike bets jump

forecast.analysis: The first full hour after the scheduled reopen. Tail is held at 13 because conditional continuation of an opening gap is the realistic adverse scenario here, though that structure would be unobserved at publication time. Stress eases to 45 once an initial reopen price has been discovered and part of the backlog is priced.
drivers: First full hour after the scheduled reopen; structure still unobserved
Conditional gap continuation is the main adverse scenario for this hour
Stress eases once an initial reopen price has been discovered
Tail of 13 remains far below the 25 block threshold

forecast.analysis: Tokyo cash trade would begin around this hour, adding a second liquidity pool to the Sunday reopen. Tail is published slightly lower at 12 on the assumption that broader participation makes two-way flow more likely; that assumption would be invalidated if early retracements were to fail and price were to hold near a session extreme.
drivers: Tokyo cash open adds a second liquidity pool to the reopen tape
Broader participation conditionally favours two-way flow
Stated invalidation: failed early retracements holding near an extreme
Confidence returns to the solid band as live discovery resumes

The scheduled halt continues through this hour; the mode is normal for want of classifiable structure and only Confidence moves as the reference tape ages.
Scores repeat unchanged during the halt, with Stress 25 anchored on the unresolved September policy debate rather than on any observable stress in the tape.
Front-end concentration of Friday's yield move, with the 10-year adding only about 4 basis points, limits the Tail case for this halt hour.
Friday's semiconductor-led drag against a flat Dow and two higher sectors is an internal split, which is scored as Stress rather than Tail.
Gold's 2.88 percent decline is a coherent cross-asset signature, and coherent context cannot substitute for the absent NQ price path in this halt hour.
